Customising and saving diagrams

Source: vignettes/articles/customisation.Rmd
customisation.Rmd

Colour palettes

Both diagram functions accept a palette as either:

  • A palette name supported by diagram_colours() (viridis or HCL palettes), e.g. "magma", "plasma", "Reds"
  • A character vector of hex colours, e.g. c("#FFFFFF", "#FFFF00", "#FF0000")

Run ?diagram_colours to see supported palette names, and use test_colour() to visualise a named or custom palette before applying it.

test_colour("magma")
test_colour(c("#FFFFFF", "#FFFF00", "#FF0000"))

Heatmap display options

heatmap_diagram() supports:

  • View: "front", "back", or "both"
  • Diagram sex: "male" or "female"
  • Opacity control
  • Optional labels (region names) and/or values
  • Optional legend scale
heatmap_diagram(df, "boxing", "both", sex = "female",
                opacity = 0.8, show_scale = TRUE)

See ?heatmap_diagram for the full argument list.

Sunburst display options

sunburst_diagram_echarts() supports:

  • Colour per tissue type, with pathology slices automatically lightened
  • Optional exclusion of “Unspecified”/“Non-specific” tissue rows
  • depth = 1 to show only the tissue-level ring
  • Label/leader-line, radius, font and title tuning
sunburst_diagram_echarts(df_sb, "boxing", depth = 1,
                         plot_title = "Tissue types only")

See ?sunburst_diagram_echarts for the full argument list.

Saving diagrams

save_diagram(plot, file, width = ...) detects whether plot is a heatmap or a sunburst and applies the matching export logic, deriving the height from the width at the correct aspect ratio automatically:

p_heat <- heatmap_diagram(df, "boxing", "front", sex = "male")
save_diagram(p_heat, file = "heatmap.png", width = 1600, units = "px")

p_sun <- sunburst_diagram_echarts(df_sb, "boxing")
save_diagram(p_sun, file = "sunburst.png", width = 1200)

Heatmaps are saved via ggplot2::ggsave() (PNG, PDF, SVG, JPG, …). Sunbursts are saved via a headless Chromium browser through the optional chromote package (PNG, JPG, PDF), so install chromote and base64enc if you need sunburst file export.
